name: Hotmon and NetProvider DPRK IT-worker communications tools

attribution.legal_posture: Gordon identifies Hotmon as a HopanaTech tool used by DPRK IT workers and NetProvider as a functionally similar variant

ttps: Require key-file and password material for access
Reuse functionally similar software under a different interface/name
Use specialized peer-to-peer communication software among IT workers or with operators in the DPRK
caveats: The researcher lacked the key/password, so behavior was inferred from static inspection and community context.

images.caption: Slide showing Hotmon and NetProvider key/password interfaces.

infrastructure.value: WinPcap-based peer-to-peer communication applications requiring a key file and password

sources.support: Official conference-channel recording of Daniel Gordon’s research into backdoored software distributed to DPRK IT workers and a low-confidence attribution assessment for the HEPTA-X cluster
sources.locator: 01:45–09:31 Hopana Tech/Hotmon findings; 09:31–18:55 HEPTA-X investigation and attribution; 18:55–20:23 takeaways
